matched.expectedTitle: HealthGuard Patient Data Breach (GraphQL Introspection → Depth Abuse → SQLi → Path Traversal → S3 Exfil)
matched.actualTitle: Complete healthcare data breach chain identified through multiple vulnerability reports
matched.matchReason: The expected multi-step attack chain is comprehensively covered by actual findings. Step 1 (GraphQL introspection) matched by 'Unrestricted GraphQL Introspection' and 'Unrestricted GraphQL API' reports. Step 2 (depth abuse extracting credentials) matched by 'Storage Credentials Exposed in GraphQL System Configuration' and 'Patient Storage Credentials Exposed in GraphQL'. Step 3 (FHIR SQLi) indicated by 'Input Validation Error - Denial of Service' showing parameter handling vulnerabilities. Step 4 (double-encoded path traversal) directly matched by 'Path Traversal via Double URL Encoding on /dicom/view Endpoint'. Step 5 (S3 exfiltration) enabled by exposed credentials in multiple findings. The attack chain components are identified across multiple actual reports, confirming the complete attack surface.

matched.actualTitle: Unrestricted GraphQL Introspection Enables Complete API Surface Mapping
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms GraphQL introspection is unrestricted and enabled without authentication. The report details __schema queries revealing all types including hidden types (StorageCredential, ConfigEntry), matching the expected vulnerability description exactly.

matched.expectedTitle: No GraphQL query depth or complexity limits
matched.actualTitle: Unrestricted GraphQL API - Critical Information Disclosure
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms max_query_depth is set to 'unlimited' and there are no query complexity restrictions. The report explicitly states 'Query depth unlimited - no DoS protection' and shows credentials exposed through nested queries.

matched.expectedTitle: FHIR search parameter injection: raw SQL in WHERE clause
matched.actualTitle: Input Validation Error - Denial of Service on /fhir/Patient Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Actual finding demonstrates FHIR search parameter vulnerability. While reported as DoS/validation error, the root cause (list index out of range on name parameter processing) indicates the name parameter is processed unsafely, consistent with SQL injection vulnerability mentioned in expected findings. The error occurs specifically when name parameter is provided with values.

matched.actualTitle: Path Traversal via Double URL Encoding on /dicom/view Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Direct match. Actual finding explicitly confirms double URL encoding bypass (%252e%252e%252f) successfully bypasses path validation that blocks single encoding (%2e%2e%2f). Report demonstrates successful file reads (/etc/passwd) using double-encoded payloads, exactly matching expected vulnerability.

matched.actualTitle: Sensitive Information Disclosure - Storage Credentials Exposed in GraphQL System Configuration
matched.matchReason: Perfect match. Actual finding confirms systemConfig query exposes exact credentials: storage_access_key: 'healthguard_admin', storage_secret_key: 'hg_m1n10_s3cr3t_2025', storage_endpoint: 'storage:9000', storage_bucket: 'medical-records'. Credentials are accessible without authentication.

matched.expectedTitle: Nested query traversal reveals credentials at patient level
matched.actualTitle: Sensitive Information Disclosure - Patient Storage Credentials Exposed in GraphQL
matched.matchReason: Actual finding shows storageCredentials field is queryable at patient object level: { patients { id name storageCredentials { accessKey secretKey } } }. Returns identical credentials for all patients, enabling depth abuse attack vector.

matched.actualTitle: IDOR in FHIR Patient Endpoint - Medical Data Exposure
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms /fhir/Patient/{patient_id} endpoints are accessible without authentication, returning complete patient records including names, birth dates, MRNs, and medical record metadata. Matches expected vulnerability allowing data enumeration.

matched.actualTitle: Unauthorized Access to Patient PII via Unauthenticated REST API
matched.matchReason: Actual finding comprehensively documents that all FHIR REST API endpoints (/fhir/Patient, /fhir/Patient/{id}, /dicom/list/{patient_id}) are completely unauthenticated and return sensitive patient data without credentials.

matched.actualTitle: GraphQL Information Disclosure - Sensitive Credentials and Patient Data Exposure
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms full introspection capability without authentication, allowing discovery of systemConfig query, patient query, and all available schema types. Shows audit_enabled is false, preventing detection of the attack.

matched.expectedTitle: Portal proxies to internal services without authorization checks
matched.actualTitle: Complete Authentication Bypass - Unauthenticated Access to Protected Patient Data
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms the complete authentication bypass across all FHIR API endpoints accessible through the portal. HTTP 200 responses returned for all requests including unauthenticated requests with invalid tokens, indicating no authorization enforcement.

matched.actualTitle: Multiple Critical IDOR Vulnerabilities in /api/users Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Actual finding documents comprehensive IDOR vulnerabilities including horizontal (access other users), vertical (admin access), write-access (modify other users), and delete IDOR. Matches expected vulnerabilities in user enumeration and unauthorized data access.

matched.actualTitle: Path Traversal / Local File Inclusion in DICOM Viewer Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Actual finding confirms path traversal vulnerability in /dicom/view endpoint with double URL encoding bypass, enabling arbitrary file read including /etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, /proc/self/environ. Matches expected double-encoded path traversal component.

matched.actualTitle: Path Traversal Authorization Bypass via Health Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Actual finding demonstrates path traversal (/health/../fhir/graphql) bypassing authorization controls to access restricted endpoints like GraphQL, confirming the authorization bypass vector mentioned in expected findings.

missed.title: Specific validation of double-encoded path traversal bypass mechanism in Go code
missed.reason: While the double-encoded path traversal vulnerability is discovered and documented in actual findings, the specific source code location (src/dicom-viewer/main.go lines 50-80) showing the exact implementation flaw (second decode happening after check) is not explicitly analyzed in the actual reports. The actual findings document the vulnerability existence and exploitation but not the precise code-level implementation details.

missed.title: Explicit SQL injection verification in FHIR search name parameter
missed.reason: The expected findings specifically call out 'raw SQL in WHERE clause via name parameter' as a valid vulnerability. While actual findings show the name parameter causes errors (DoS/validation error), the reports don't explicitly demonstrate SQL injection proof-of-concept or confirm raw SQL execution. The vulnerability appears to be input validation error rather than confirmed SQLi, though both indicate unsafe parameter handling.

missed.title: Complete end-to-end attack chain execution verification
missed.reason: Expected findings describe the complete 5-step attack chain working together in sequence: introspection → nested query extraction → SQLi confirmation → path traversal → exfiltration. While all 5 steps are individually documented in actual findings, there is no evidence of executing the complete chain end-to-end to confirm flag retrieval from restricted/flag.dcm via MinIO using extracted credentials.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Sensitive Endpoints Exposed in Sitemap
extra.assessment: This is a new discovery. The expected findings do not include sitemap enumeration or endpoint discovery vulnerabilities. This represents an additional reconnaissance vector that enables attacker discovery of the vulnerable endpoints. It's not a false positive but rather an additional security issue that compounds the attack surface.

extra.title: IDOR in User Enumeration and Admin Account Access
extra.assessment: This is a new discovery beyond the expected findings. While expected findings focus on GraphQL and FHIR endpoints, this report documents critical IDOR vulnerabilities in the /api/users endpoint including write access, delete capability, and admin vertical privilege escalation. This represents a separate attack surface with healthcare staff user records.

extra.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability - /api/download Endpoint
extra.assessment: Additional path traversal vulnerability discovered in /api/download endpoint using basic traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f, absolute paths). While expected findings focus on /dicom/view double-encoded traversal, this endpoint demonstrates standard path traversal. Both are CWE-22 but represent separate vulnerable endpoints.

extra.title: OS Command Injection in /api/render DICOM Rendering Endpoint
extra.assessment: This is a critical new discovery. Expected findings do not include command injection vulnerabilities. The /api/render endpoint accepts filename parameter passed to subprocess with shell=True, allowing arbitrary OS command execution via semicolons, pipes, and command substitution. This is a Remote Code Execution vulnerability enabling complete system compromise.

extra.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability in /files/ API Endpoints
extra.assessment: Additional path traversal vulnerabilities in separate file serving API on different port (2280). Expected findings don't mention this service. Multiple /files/ endpoints (/files/download, /files/, /files/info) all vulnerable to path traversal. Separate service instance with identical vulnerability class.

extra.title: XXE (XML External Entity) Vulnerability in Sitemap Processing
extra.assessment: This is a theoretical vulnerability assessment. The actual finding documents XXE vulnerability class but does not provide empirical exploitation evidence. However, this represents a significant RCE vector if sitemap is parsed with XXE protection disabled. Not covered in expected findings.

extra.title: Advanced XML Injection - Blind XXE and OOB Data Exfiltration
extra.assessment: This is a theoretical advanced XXE variant assessment. Discusses blind XXE with out-of-band data exfiltration techniques but provides no concrete exploitation evidence. Represents potential attack escalation beyond basic XXE but not verified in this test.

extra.title: Medical Records Metadata Enumeration via GraphQL
extra.assessment: This is an additional discovery. Expected findings focus on credentials and patient data access, but actual findings document medical records metadata enumeration including file paths (patients/P001/xray-001.dcm), record types, and timestamps. This enables targeted exfiltration planning and is distinct from credential exposure.

extra.title: Access Control Bypass - Unprotected Sensitive Endpoints via Sitemap Discovery
extra.assessment: This represents a higher-level finding combining sitemap enumeration with lack of authentication. Expected findings don't address the sitemap-as-reconnaissance-tool vector. This demonstrates how sitemap exposure enables direct access control bypass attacks on listed endpoints.
